_meta.title: Tier 2b — granular ingredient/substance detail for danger-zone categories
_meta.purpose: The DEEP layer beneath the category (Tier 1) and attribute-trigger (Tier 2) files: specific prohibited ingredients, named substances, concentration limits, and Amazon-specific sub-policies for the categories the user actually touches. This is the 'don't miss the necessary detail' layer.
_meta.confidence_note: From FDA (21 CFR 700.11-700.35), EU/UK Cosmetics Regulation Annexes, and Amazon sub-policies, accurate as of compile date. Ingredient lists evolve; EU/UK lists are longer and stricter than US. Definitive per-product answer = Seller Central Apply-to-Sell + a qualified safety assessor (CPSR).
_meta.usage_rule: Sourcing alarm + listing warning. If a product's ingredient list (from competitor data / specs) contains a prohibited substance -> flag. NEVER strip a true ingredient from copy to conceal — that is falsification, worse than the restriction.
_meta.design_principle_confirmed: EU/UK is the harder constraint. A formula that clears EU/UK almost always clears US, but NOT the reverse. So for UK marketplace, apply the stricter EU/UK Annex rules.

cosmetic_prohibited_ingredients.note: Scan competitor ingredient lists / product specs for these. Presence = restricted or prohibited depending on substance and marketplace.

outright_or_tightly_restricted.name: Mercury compounds
outright_or_tightly_restricted.status: prohibited except eye-area at <=0.0065% when no alternative preservative — effectively prohibited

outright_or_tightly_restricted.name: Hydroquinone
outright_or_tightly_restricted.status: OTC skin-lightening = unapproved drug (not GRASE), reclassified prescription-only. Effectively prohibited as OTC cosmetic.

eu_uk_prohibited.regulation: UK Cosmetics Regulation 2020 (SI 2020/1466) / EU 1223/2009 Annexes II-VI
eu_uk_prohibited.note: EU/UK bans are far broader (~1600+ substances in Annex II). Key ones sellers hit:

key_bans.name: Hydroquinone
key_bans.status: banned for general cosmetic use in EU/UK

key_bans.name: 5 parabens (isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl-, pentyl-)
key_bans.status: banned EU 2014 (methyl/ethylparaben still allowed with limits)

amazon_skin_lightener_policy.note: Amazon has a SPECIFIC skin-lightener / whitening product policy — separate from general cosmetics. Products must demonstrate:
requirements: Third-party GMP compliance from an accredited body/scheme
Heavy metals testing including mercury testing
Verification of FDA product registration (FDA form 5067)
amazon_skin_lightener_policy.targets_flag: FDA notes these are often marketed to Asian/African/Latino/Middle Eastern communities and often DON'T declare mercury/hydroquinone on the label — so ingredient absence from a label is NOT proof of safety.

cosmetic_prohibited_ingredients.sunscreen_note: Sunscreens are DRUGS (not cosmetics) per FDA. SPF claims move a product into OTC drug regulation. UK/EU treat sunscreen as cosmetic but with strict UV-filter Annex VI limits.

claims_that_convert_to_drug.note: These CLAIMS flip a cosmetic into a regulated OTC DRUG = instant restriction. Ties to claims screener.
